subject: Aurora perf discovery: streaming constraints, SLO levers & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Nadeem <samira@auroramldev.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@auroramldev.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Aurora perf discovery: streaming constraints, SLO levers & next steps

Hi Samira / Alex,

Thanks for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we have clear next steps from the Redwood side.

Call highlights (short):
- Workload: low-latency streaming transcriptions + short completion prompts (avg prompt 120 tokens, outputs ~80 tokens) across mobile clients.
- Traffic profile: regional spikes to 350 qps sustained for 10s, baseline 45 qps.
- SLO target: P95 generation latency <= 220ms tokenized (end-to-end for 1-stream incremental tokens) and tail protection for bursts.
- Concurrency: target 1.5k concurrent streams with reasonably consistent per-stream FPS.

Key technical constraints you mentioned:
- Must preserve partial-token streaming (server-sent events) — cannot buffer full responses and then push.
- Client requires <250ms first-token latency for 92% of requests.
- Audited tenant isolation; logs and audit trails required for SOC-compat work.

Redwood follow-ups (what we will deliver):
1) A short performance plan mapping levers to cost: continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles (FP16 vs int8/4), and model variant recommendations (gpt-like-medium vs large).
2) An initial sizing estimate for Dedicated capacity to meet P95 latency at both baseline and 10x spike.
3) A small proof-of-concept runbook to validate streaming-first-token latencies (we propose a 2-hour synthetic test using your sample traces).
4) Checklist for SOC/logging items you flagged.

Action items + owners:
- Karthik: deliver initial perf plan and cost delta matrix by EOD 2027-05-04. (attached: product requirements spreadsheet with the workload snapshot)
- Ben Carter (cc): provide Dedicated sizing sketch and concurrency/throughput tradeoffs.
- Alex / Samira: share 48h of representative traffic traces and a sample audio stream (or replay endpoint) so we can run the POC.

Open questions for you (please confirm):
- Are partial tokens allowed to be re-ordered slightly for batching benefits, or do you need strict in-order per-chunk delivery?
- Any hard constraint on model family? If Aurora is open to a smaller model variant for latency-critical paths, we can save ~30-50% CPU/GPU cost.

I attached the requirements sheet and recorded the call — let us know when you can share traces. Once we have them Ben and I will sketch a small runbook for the synthetic validation.

Thanks again — Karthik

--

Thanks Karthik — that summary is spot on. A couple clarifications:

1) Streaming requirements: we need in-order, partial-token delivery for the UI — small reordering of micro-chunks is acceptable as long as UI reassembly is deterministic.
2) Model family: preference for our vendor-tuned medium-sized model for initial rollout, but open to switching to a quantized variant if quality checks (WER and hallucination rate) are in-range.
3) Security: audit logs and KMS integration are must-haves; we can start with a read-only list of required fields (we'll drop that into the Drive folder).

We uploaded the trace bundle to the Drive folder (see link you included) and added a short README describing peak vs baseline windows. Alex will schedule the replay endpoint for you by EOD tomorrow.

Budget note: we have an internal cap for the POC phase (~$12k in infra credits) and would like Redwood to provide an estimate for the pilot so we can get procurement aligned.

Samira

Karthik / team — quick sketch from ops side (high level bullets, will follow with a spreadsheet):

1) Continuous batching approach:
- Use 5ms micro-window batching for best latency/cost tradeoff. That yields ~10-25% batching efficiency vs 10ms but helps first-token latencies; we can tune to 10ms window if traffic is bursty.
- Prefix/KV caching: since many streams are repeated short prompts, enabling prefix caching should reduce compute by ~18-30% for baseline traffic. Requires a small Redis cache or in-host cache on Dedicated nodes.

2) Quantization profiles & model variants:
- Baseline: vendor medium model FP16 — expected P95 ~180-220ms under baseline 45 qps with 200 concurrent streams on a single A100-like node (synthetic estimate).
- Cost-cutting: int8 quantization reduces GPU memory and increases throughput ~1.6x; expect P95 penalty ~+10-20ms in worst-case; int4 experimental can double throughput but increases tail variance and requires QA.
- Fallback plan: configure routing policy to fallback to quantized-medium under spike > steady-state threshold; prioritize critical customer lanes to non-quantized nodes.

3) Sizing sketch for their stated 1.5k concurrent streams at 350 qps spikes:
- Pilot (up to 48h replay): 2 x rtx6000-equivalent nodes on Dedicated reserved preemptible to stay under $12k (approx). That will let us validate first-token latency at moderate load.
- Production baseline to meet P95 SLO at scale: ~6-8 A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscaling and cache warmers; exact number depends on final model choice and quantization.

4) Blocking items:
- Need 48h traces + a replay endpoint and the sample audio.
- SOC items: list of required logs and KMS integration details from Aurora (they said they'd drop README).

I'll assemble a short cost delta table (FP16 vs int8 vs int4) and model recommendation by EOD for Karthik to pass to Samira. If we have to hit a sub-$12k pilot, recommend: 24h of replay, preemptible Dedicated, and run with FP16 + prefix caching to keep latencies stable.
